package connect

// ResultOf computes the winner (or lack thereof) of a game of Hex / Polygon.
//
// The board is a parallelogram of hexagonal cells given as a slice of rows.
// Each row is a string of cells: 'X', 'O' or '.' (empty). Because the board
// is a parallelogram, each row is shifted one cell to the right relative to
// the row above it.
//
// Player 'O' is assigned the top and bottom sides and wins by connecting them;
// player 'X' is assigned the left and right sides and wins by connecting them.
// A connection is a path of a player's own cells between the two assigned
// sides. At most one player can ever connect, so we report the one who does.
func ResultOf(lines []string) (string, error) {
	if len(lines) == 0 {
		return "", nil
	}

	height := len(lines)
	width := 0
	for _, l := range lines {
		if len(l) > width {
			width = len(l)
		}
	}

	// cellAt returns the cell at (row, col), or 0 when out of bounds.
	cellAt := func(row, col int) rune {
		if row < 0 || row >= height || col < 0 || col >= len(lines[row]) {
			return 0
		}
		return rune(lines[row][col])
	}

	neighbours := [6][2]int{
		{0, -1}, {0, 1},   // left, right
		{-1, 0}, {-1, 1},  // upper-left, upper-right
		{1, 0}, {1, -1},   // lower-right, lower-left
	}

	// connected reports whether the player has a connected path of their own
	// cells between their two assigned sides.
	connected := func(player rune) bool {
		onStart := func(r, c int) bool {
			if player == 'O' {
				return r == 0
			}
			return c == 0
		}
		onEnd := func(r, c int) bool {
			if player == 'O' {
				return r == height-1
			}
			return c == width-1
		}

		visited := make([][]bool, height)
		for i := range visited {
			visited[i] = make([]bool, len(lines[i]))
		}

		var stack [][2]int
		for r := 0; r < height; r++ {
			for c := 0; c < len(lines[r]); c++ {
				if cellAt(r, c) == player && onStart(r, c) {
					visited[r][c] = true
					stack = append(stack, [2]int{r, c})
				}
